# Finding ∫ 2x⁴ cos(2x) dx

## Setting Up Integration by Parts (Tabular Method)

I'll use the tabular method, differentiating the polynomial and integrating the trig function:

| Sign | Derivative of 2x⁴ | Integral of cos(2x) |
|------|-------------------|---------------------|
| +    | 2x⁴              | (1/2)sin(2x)       |
| −    | 8x³              | −(1/4)cos(2x)      |
| +    | 24x²             | −(1/8)sin(2x)      |
| −    | 48x              | (1/16)cos(2x)      |
| +    | 48               | (1/32)sin(2x)      |

## Multiplying Diagonals with Signs

$$+2x^4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}\sin(2x) = x^4 \sin(2x)$$

$$-8x^3 \cdot \left(-\tfrac{1}{4}\cos(2x)\right) = 2x^3 \cos(2x)$$

$$+24x^2 \cdot \left(-\tfrac{1}{8}\sin(2x)\right) = -3x^2 \sin(2x)$$

$$-48x \cdot \tfrac{1}{16}\cos(2x) = -3x \cos(2x)$$

$$+48 \cdot \tfrac{1}{32}\sin(2x) = \tfrac{3}{2}\sin(2x)$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
- d/dx[x⁴sin(2x)] = 4x³sin(2x) + 2x⁴cos(2x)
- d/dx[2x³cos(2x)] = 6x²cos(2x) − 4x³sin(2x)
- d/dx[−3x²sin(2x)] = −6xsin(2x) − 6x²cos(2x)
- d/dx[−3xcos(2x)] = −3cos(2x) + 6xsin(2x)
- d/dx[(3/2)sin(2x)] = 3cos(2x)

All terms cancel except **2x⁴cos(2x)** ✓

<answer>x**4*sin(2*x) + 2*x**3*cos(2*x) - 3*x**2*sin(2*x) - 3*x*cos(2*x) + 3*sin(2*x)/2 + C</answer>
